notable_absence.finding: The 'Regenerating Default Certificates' section documents an operator's only two ways found anywhere in this batch to stop a certificate chain being trusted before its own expiry: (1) regenerate everything (a new self-signed root, cascading to all node certificates), or (2) delete an old root CA from the trust store once no node certificate in use still depends on it. Neither is a per-certificate revocation - the deletion path is explicitly blocked while ANY dependent node certificate remains in use ('You cannot delete a certificate if it has signed one or more node certificates that are in use in the cluster.'). A third occurrence of the same batch-wide gap this round keeps finding: the corpus has no concept anywhere for revoking a single compromised certificate without regenerating or deleting its whole issuing chain.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest instance in the batch of the round's hypothesized finding: three REST admin actions central to certificate lifecycle management on Couchbase Server - loadTrustedCAs, reloadCertificate, and the regenerate-all-certificates endpoint - are named and used repeatedly here (curl examples for each) but appear in NO other extraction record in the corpus, including learn/security/certificates.md, this same batch's own conceptual-overview page for certificates. The reference/conceptual layer describes certificates as things with properties and relationships (root signs node, node presents itself, trust store validates); it never describes the operational act of getting a certificate file from a workstation onto a running cluster node. That whole staging-and-activation mechanism - the inbox directory, its required filenames and permissions, and the load/reload REST calls that consume it - exists only on this administration-procedure page.
